lines: Start from the simplest agent design that works; before adding a planner, a critic or another agent, compare both variants on the task set and report success rate, steps and tokens per task, since every agent added is more cost and one more point of failure.

group: A planner, a critic or one more agent is added only when a measure on a task set shows the simpler design fails.
lines: Trying a richer agent pattern (planning, branches, several agents) is welcome without a prior measure; keep each experiment behind a switch and say what it costs in steps and tokens.

group: A second pass checks the agent’s output before it is returned, even though it doubles the latency.
lines: Before the agent returns code, a query or a report, run a review step that checks it against the goal and sends it back for one bounded correction; where a deterministic check exists (tests, a parser, a schema), use it instead of a model as the critic.

group: A second pass checks the agent’s output before it is returned, even though it doubles the latency.
lines: Do not add a self-review or critic step to the agent: it doubles latency and the critic can be wrong; validate outputs with deterministic checks only.

group: The agent loop is:
label: Written by hand on the model provider’s SDK
lines: The agent loop is written by hand on the model provider’s SDK: keep the loop, the tool dispatch, the retries and the traces explicit in the project’s own code, and do not add an agent framework.

group: The agent loop is:
label: Run by an agent framework
lines: The agent runs on {value}: use its primitives for the loop, state and tools instead of re-implementing them, check its current documentation before using an API since it changes fast, and do not add a second agent framework.

group: The framework or the provider’s SDK stays behind our own interfaces, so it can be replaced.
lines: Import the agent framework or the model provider’s SDK only in one adapter module; tools, prompts and business code depend on the project’s own types for messages, tool calls and results, never on the library’s.

group: The framework or the provider’s SDK stays behind our own interfaces, so it can be replaced.
lines: Use the types and helpers of the agent framework or the model provider’s SDK directly where they are needed; do not wrap them in an abstraction layer of our own.

group: Every run of the agent is bounded by:
label: A maximum number of steps
lines: Never write an agent loop without a hard step limit: a named constant (typically 10 to 30 depending on the task), and a run that reaches it ends with an explicit "step budget exhausted" outcome, not a silent return.

group: Every run of the agent is bounded by:
label: A token budget per task
lines: Count input and output tokens across the steps of a task and stop the run when its budget is spent; each turn resends the whole history, so 10 steps over 20k tokens of history already cost 200k input tokens.

group: Every run of the agent is bounded by:
label: An overall time limit per task
lines: Give every agent task an overall deadline, pass its cancellation signal to the model call and to every tool, and end the run cleanly when it fires.

group: Every run of the agent is bounded by:
label: A timeout on each tool call
lines: Run every tool call with its own timeout, and turn a timeout into a tool error the model can read rather than a hung run.

group: When a tool fails:
label: The error goes back to the model, which corrects itself
lines: Never hide a tool failure from the model: catch it and return it as the result of that tool call, with a short message saying what failed and what to change, so the model can correct itself; never return a stack trace or a secret in it.

group: When a tool fails:
label: The code retries transient failures, then gives the error to the model
lines: Retry a transient tool failure (timeout, 429, 5xx) in code a bounded number of times with backoff, then return the error as the result of that tool call with a short actionable message; never retry a validation or permission error.

group: When a tool fails:
label: The run stops with an error
lines: A tool failure ends the run: stop the loop, record the failed call and its error in the trace, and surface a clear error to the caller instead of letting the model continue.

group: As a run gets longer, its history is:
label: Cut to the most recent turns
lines: Keep the system prompt, the task and the most recent turns in the context and drop older ones; never cut between a tool call and its result, and do not rely on the start of a long conversation still being visible.

group: As a run gets longer, its history is:
label: Summarised progressively
lines: When the history nears its token threshold, replace the oldest turns with a summary that keeps the goal, the decisions made and the ids obtained; never cut between a tool call and its result, and keep the raw turns in storage.

group: As a run gets longer, its history is:
label: Kept, with old tool results shortened
lines: Keep the turns of a run but shorten tool results once they are a few steps old (a cap on size, with a note that the output was cut); cap the size of a result when the tool returns it rather than injecting a whole payload.

group: As a run gets longer, its history is:
label: Kept whole (runs are short)
lines: The history of a run is sent whole: keep runs short, cap the size of every tool result when the tool returns it, and fail clearly before the context window is exceeded instead of sending a request that will be refused.

group: We select what enters the context rather than count on a large context window.
lines: Do not treat a large context window as memory: inject only what the current step needs (the relevant records, the top passages, the fields used), since quality drops when the context is long and noisy and every token is paid again at each step.

group: We select what enters the context rather than count on a large context window.
lines: Whole documents and full tool results may be put in the context when they fit; still count tokens before the call and fail clearly when the window would be exceeded.

group: While the agent runs, its caller receives:
label: Each step as it happens (text, tool calls, results)
lines: Emit a typed event for each step of a run (text delta, tool call started, tool result, final answer, error); assemble a streamed tool call completely before validating and running it, never execute partial arguments.

group: While the agent runs, its caller receives:
label: Only the final answer
lines: A run returns only its final answer: do not add streaming of intermediate steps unasked, and keep the steps in the trace instead.

group: While the agent runs, its caller receives:
label: Nothing: the run is a background job whose status is read later
lines: Run the agent as a background job, not inside the request: persist the state of the run after each step so it can be resumed or cancelled, and expose its status and result through the existing job mechanism.

group: The steps of the agent run on:
label: The same model for every step
lines: Every step of the agent uses the single model set in configuration: do not route steps to another model unasked.

group: The steps of the agent run on:
label: A small model for simple steps, a stronger one for planning and hard ones
lines: Send simple steps (classification, extraction, routing) to the small model and keep the stronger or reasoning model for planning and hard steps; each kind of step names its model tier, never a model id.

group: The stable start of the prompt (system prompt, tool definitions) is:
label: Cached with the provider’s prompt caching
lines: Keep the cached prefix byte-stable: system prompt and tool definitions first and in a fixed order, no date, id or per-user value inside it, and anything that varies appended after it; check cached-token counts in the usage after changing it.

group: The stable start of the prompt (system prompt, tool definitions) is:
label: Not cached
lines: Prompt caching is not used: do not add cache markers or restructure prompts for it unasked.

group: The agent’s system prompt always states:
label: The goal and what counts as done
lines: In an agent’s system prompt, state the goal, the constraints and an explicit success criterion the agent can check before it answers; never leave it at "do your best".

group: The agent’s system prompt always states:
label: Who the user is and which business rules apply
lines: Give the agent’s system prompt the context it cannot guess: who the user is, which data it works on and the business rules that apply, in the exact vocabulary of the domain with house terms defined.

group: The agent’s system prompt always states:
label: When to stop and ask a person
lines: Say in the agent’s system prompt when it must stop and ask a person (missing information, an action outside its scope, repeated failure) instead of guessing or retrying.

group: The agent’s system prompt always states:
label: The length and format of the answer
lines: State the expected length and format of the final answer (JSON, list, Markdown) in the agent’s system prompt.

group: The agent’s system prompt always states:
label: One to three examples
lines: Fix an output format in the agent’s system prompt with one to three input and output examples rather than a longer description.

group: The parameters of a tool are defined with:
label: A schema library (Zod, Pydantic…) that also gives the JSON Schema
lines: Define the parameters of a tool once with the project’s schema library: derive the JSON Schema sent to the model from it and parse the model’s arguments with the same schema before the tool runs.

group: The parameters of a tool are defined with:
label: JSON Schema written by hand
lines: Write the parameters of a tool as JSON Schema with `required`, `enum` for closed sets and a description per property, and validate the model’s arguments against that same schema before the tool runs.

group: The parameters of a tool are defined with:
label: The agent framework’s own tool declarations
lines: Declare a tool with the agent framework’s own tool API, typed parameters and descriptions included, and let it validate the arguments; do not hand-write a parallel JSON Schema.

group: We keep the set of tools small, each with a precise name and a description of when to use it.
lines: Before adding a tool, check that an existing one cannot cover the need; give each tool an explicit verb-first name and a description saying when to use it and when not to, and ask before growing the tool set.

group: We keep the set of tools small, each with a precise name and a description of when to use it.
lines: Add a tool whenever a capability is missing; still give it an explicit name and a description saying when to use it, and make sure it does not overlap an existing one.

group: A tool that changes something is idempotent, so that a repeated call cannot do it twice.
lines: Make every tool that writes idempotent: derive an idempotency key from the run and the tool call, or check the current state first, so a retry or a repeated call by the model creates, sends or charges only once.

group: A tool that changes something is idempotent, so that a repeated call cannot do it twice.
lines: Tools are not required to be idempotent: never retry a tool that writes automatically, and say in its description that calling it again repeats the action.

group: With the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the project:
label: Connects its agent to MCP servers
lines: The agent gets external tools through MCP servers: discover them with `tools/list`, pass them to the model like local tools, and apply the same validation, permissions, timeouts and result size caps to them.

group: With the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the project:
label: Exposes its own MCP server
lines: The project exposes an MCP server: add a capability as a tool (an action), a resource (readable data) or a prompt with the official SDK, with a typed input schema, and apply the same authorization as the rest of the API.

group: With the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the project:
label: Does both
lines: The project both exposes an MCP server and connects its agent to MCP servers: build both sides with the official SDK, give every tool a typed input schema, and apply the project’s validation, permissions and timeouts on each side.

group: With the Model Context Protocol (MCP), the project:
label: Does not use it
lines: MCP is not used: define tools in the project’s own code and do not add an MCP server or client unasked.

group: MCP servers are reached over:
label: stdio (a local subprocess)
lines: MCP runs over stdio: a server writes only protocol messages to standard output and logs to standard error, and it runs with the rights of the user who launched it, so keep what it can reach narrow.

group: MCP servers are reached over:
label: Streamable HTTP (a remote server)
lines: MCP runs over Streamable HTTP: authenticate every request, scope each call to the tenant of its token, rate limit it, and never fall back to an unauthenticated endpoint.

group: MCP servers are reached over:
label: Both
lines: MCP runs over stdio locally and Streamable HTTP remotely: keep tool logic independent of the transport, log to standard error under stdio, and authenticate, scope to the tenant and rate limit every HTTP request.

group: A third-party MCP server is connected to the agent:
label: Never
lines: Never connect the agent to a third-party MCP server: use only the project’s own servers and tools, or stop and say what is missing.

group: A third-party MCP server is connected to the agent:
label: After I reviewed its source and its rights
lines: Ask before connecting the agent to a third-party MCP server: say who publishes it, what it can run and reach, and pin it to an exact version; it executes code and injects text into the context.

group: A third-party MCP server is connected to the agent:
label: When the assistant finds one useful, and tells me
lines: A third-party MCP server may be connected when it clearly beats writing the tool: pick a maintained one, pin it to an exact version, expose only the tools the agent needs and say what was added.

group: Between sessions, the agent remembers through:
label: Nothing: each session starts fresh
lines: The agent keeps nothing between sessions: do not add a memory store, a profile or stored summaries unasked, and build each context from the current conversation and tools only.

group: Between sessions, the agent remembers through:
label: A structured profile (stable facts and preferences)
lines: Long-term memory is a structured profile with a fixed schema: write a fact to it only once the user or a tool result confirmed it, never what the agent assumed, and inject only the fields relevant to the task.

group: Between sessions, the agent remembers through:
label: A log of past episodes, searched by meaning
lines: Long-term memory is a dated log of episodes (actions, results, decisions) with embeddings: store what happened, not what the agent assumed, retrieve only the few most relevant episodes for a task and inject them marked as past context.

group: Between sessions, the agent remembers through:
label: A profile and episodes
lines: Long-term memory is a structured profile for stable facts and a dated log of episodes searched by meaning: store only what the user or a tool result confirmed, never an assumption, and inject only what is relevant to the task.

group: Between sessions, the agent remembers through:
label: Something else
lines: The agent’s long-term memory is: {value}. Store only confirmed facts in it, never what the agent assumed, and inject only what is relevant to the task.

group: What the agent remembers is partitioned by:
label: User
lines: Key every memory record and every conversation by its user, and filter on that user in the query itself, on reads and writes alike; never share a memory, a summary or a cache entry between users.

group: What the agent remembers is partitioned by:
label: User and organisation
lines: Key every memory record and every conversation by user and organisation, and filter on both in the query itself, on reads and writes alike; a memory never crosses an organisation, shared caches and summaries included.

group: What the agent remembers is partitioned by:
label: Nothing: the agent serves one user or one team
lines: The agent serves a single user or team, so memory is not partitioned: do not add tenant columns or filters unasked, and say so if a change would make the agent serve several users.

group: A stored memory:
label: Expires after a set time unless it is used or confirmed again
lines: Give every stored memory a creation date and an expiry or a decaying importance score, and exclude expired ones from retrieval; never add a memory kind without its retention rule.

group: A stored memory:
label: Is kept until its user asks to delete it
lines: Memories are kept until deleted: do not add automatic expiry unasked, and keep retrieval bounded by relevance rather than by loading everything.

group: The agent gets knowledge from documents through:
label: A search tool it decides to call, and call again
lines: Retrieval is a tool the agent chooses to call: let it reformulate and search again when the passages are not enough, but cap the number of searches per task, return only the top 3 to 10 passages with their source, and have the answer cite them.

group: The agent gets knowledge from documents through:
label: One search run by the code before every answer
lines: Retrieval is one search run by the code before the model answers: keep it a fixed step, inject the top 3 to 10 passages with their source, and have the answer cite them or say that nothing relevant was found.

group: The agent gets knowledge from documents through:
label: No retrieval
lines: The agent has no document retrieval: do not add a vector store, embeddings or a search tool unasked.

group: Documents are filtered by the caller’s organisation and rights before the search, not after.
lines: Apply the caller’s organisation and access rights as a filter inside the search query itself, taken from the authenticated session and never from an argument the model wrote; never fetch first and filter the results afterwards.

group: Documents are filtered by the caller’s organisation and rights before the search, not after.
lines: Every indexed document is readable by every user of the agent: do not add per-user filters to the search unasked, and stop and ask before indexing a source that is not public to all of them.

group: Tests of a whole agent run use:
label: A scripted fake model and simulated tools
lines: Test a whole agent run with a scripted fake model that returns a fixed sequence of tool calls and answers, against simulated tools: such tests never call a model provider and must be deterministic.

group: Tests of a whole agent run use:
label: Recorded model responses, replayed
lines: Test a whole agent run by replaying recorded model responses: commit the recordings with no secret or personal data in them, re-record on purpose when a prompt or a tool changes, and never let the test suite reach a provider otherwise.

group: Tests of a whole agent run use:
label: The real model, against simulated tools
lines: Scenario tests call the real model against simulated tools: keep them in their own suite outside the unit tests, replay each case several times and assert a success rate rather than one exact output.

group: Tests of a whole agent run use:
label: No such tests
lines: There are no tests of whole agent runs: do not add a scenario harness unasked, and cover the loop logic and the tools with ordinary unit tests.

group: A scenario test of the agent checks:
label: The final answer
lines: In a scenario test, assert the final answer on what must be true of it (a field, an id, a fact it contains), not on its exact wording.

group: A scenario test of the agent checks:
label: The tools called, their arguments and their order
lines: In a scenario test, assert the trajectory and not only the final answer: which tools were called, with which arguments, in which order.

group: A scenario test of the agent checks:
label: That no useless or dangerous action was taken
lines: In a scenario test, assert what must not happen: no call to a tool that writes, deletes or sends unless the scenario requires it, and no sensitive action without the confirmation step.

group: A scenario test of the agent checks:
label: The number of steps and tokens used
lines: In a scenario test, record the steps and tokens of the run and fail when they exceed the budget set for that scenario.

group: The set of reference tasks is replayed:
label: In CI, on every change to a prompt, a tool or the model
lines: A change to a system prompt, a tool name, description or schema, or the model must pass the reference task set in CI: run it before handing back, and add a case to the set for every failure fixed.

group: The set of reference tasks is replayed:
label: By hand, before a release
lines: After changing a system prompt, a tool name, description or schema, or the model, say that the reference task set must be replayed before release, and add a case to the set for every failure fixed.

group: The set of reference tasks is replayed:
label: There is no such set yet
lines: There is no reference task set: do not build an evaluation harness unasked, and when changing a prompt or a tool description, say which behaviours were not re-checked.

group: A tool acts with:
label: The identity and rights of the user driving the agent
lines: Run every tool with the identity and rights of the user driving the agent, passed from the session by the code and never by the model; the agent never gets an admin or shared account.

group: A tool acts with:
label: A service account limited to what that tool needs
lines: Each tool uses its own service credential limited to what it needs (read-only where it only reads), and still checks in code that the user driving the agent may access the resource named in the arguments.

group: The agent waits for a person to confirm before:
label: Deleting or overwriting something
lines: A tool that deletes or overwrites never runs on the model’s request alone: the code pauses the run, shows the exact action and its target to a person and resumes only on approval; prefer a reversible operation (soft delete, archive) when one exists.

group: The agent waits for a person to confirm before:
label: Spending money
lines: A tool that costs money (creating a paid resource, a purchase, a payment) requires a person’s approval enforced in code, with the amount shown, plus a quota per user that the agent cannot exceed.

group: The agent waits for a person to confirm before:
label: Sending a message outside (e-mail, chat, SMS)
lines: A tool that sends a message outside the system (e-mail, chat, SMS) requires a person’s approval of the recipient and the content, enforced in code: sending cannot be undone.

group: The agent waits for a person to confirm before:
label: Acting on many items at once
lines: A tool call that acts on more items than the set threshold requires a person’s approval enforced in code; cap the number of items a single call may touch.

group: The agent waits for a person to confirm before:
label: Nothing: it acts alone
lines: The agent acts without human confirmation: every tool that writes then needs a hard quota, an audit log entry and, where possible, a reversible operation; say so when a new tool is irreversible.

group: Around the agent, the code enforces:
label: Tool results and fetched content marked as data, never instructions
lines: Assume the agent will be manipulated: wrap web pages, documents, e-mails and tool results in a delimiter that marks them as data, never place them in the system prompt, and never let their content alone trigger a sensitive tool.

group: Around the agent, the code enforces:
label: An isolated sandbox for code and commands the agent runs
lines: Run code and shell commands requested by the agent only in the isolated sandbox: a confined directory, no secret, no network unless allowlisted, with CPU, memory and time limits; never on the host or inside the API process.

group: Around the agent, the code enforces:
label: Secrets kept out of the context
lines: Never put a secret in a prompt, a tool description or a tool result: tools read credentials from the server environment, take a reference rather than a value as argument, and redact keys and tokens from what they return.

group: Around the agent, the code enforces:
label: An allowlist of domains the agent may reach
lines: Tools that fetch a URL or call an external service go through the domain allowlist: refuse any other host, do not follow a redirect off the list, and never build a URL from a secret or from user data the model was not asked to send.

group: Around the agent, the code enforces:
label: Personal data masked before the model and in logs
lines: Pass personal data through the project’s masking step before it reaches the model, and never write a prompt, a tool argument or a tool result to a log or a trace unmasked.

group: Around the agent, the code enforces:
label: Filters on what comes in and what goes out
lines: Keep the input and output filters on every path: a new entry point passes user input through the input filter, and anything the agent returns or sends passes the output filter before it leaves; add an adversarial case to the tests with each new tool.

group: An optimization starts from a measurement, never from a guess.
lines: Before optimizing, measure the starting point (LCP, INP, CLS, TTFB) on a throttled mobile profile, fix what weighs most first, and report the numbers before and after; never claim a gain that was not measured.
Do not chase a lab score of 100: a lab run reproduces and diagnoses a problem, real-user data says whether it matters.

group: An optimization starts from a measurement, never from a guess.
lines: Apply the usual performance practices without measuring each one; still do not add complexity (memoization, a cache, a worker) for a gain nobody measured.

group: The pages must meet:
label: The "good" Core Web Vitals thresholds (LCP ≤ 2.5 s, INP ≤ 200 ms, CLS ≤ 0.1)
lines: Keep every page within LCP 2.5 s, INP 200 ms and CLS 0.1 at the 75th percentile of real visits (not the average), with TTFB under 1.3 s; say so when a change puts one of them at risk.

group: The pages must meet:
label: No set target
lines: The project sets no performance target: do not block a change on a metric, but point out one that clearly slows loading, interaction or layout stability.

group: The pages must meet:
label: Other targets
lines: Keep every page within the project’s performance targets: {value}; say so when a change puts one of them at risk.

group: Metrics from real visits are collected with:
label: The `web-vitals` library
lines: Real-user metrics are reported with `web-vitals`: keep LCP, INP, CLS and TTFB sent to monitoring with the page and the device type, and wire a new page or route into the same reporting.

group: Metrics from real visits are collected with:
label: A monitoring service’s own agent
lines: Real-user metrics come from the monitoring service’s agent: keep it loaded on every page, do not add a second collector, and read its 75th percentile per page and device before judging a page.

group: Metrics from real visits are collected with:
label: Nothing yet
lines: No real-user metrics are collected: do not add a collector or a monitoring script unasked, and say that a lab measurement is not what users experience.

group: Performance budgets are checked in CI with:
label: Lighthouse CI
lines: Lighthouse CI enforces the budgets: a change that fails one is fixed, never merged by raising the budget or skipping the check; a new page gets its own entry in the Lighthouse CI configuration.

group: Performance budgets are checked in CI with:
label: A bundle size limit (size-limit, bundler budgets)
lines: A bundle size limit runs in CI: when a change goes over it, reduce what is shipped (split, lighter import, removal) and never raise the limit without asking.

group: Performance budgets are checked in CI with:
label: No budget in CI
lines: No budget is checked in CI: keep a page under 1,500 KB in total as a working limit, and report the change in bundle size when a change adds a dependency or a large asset.

group: Performance budgets are checked in CI with:
label: Something else
lines: Performance budgets are checked with {value}: fix a change that fails one, and never raise a budget or skip the check without asking.

group: I keep the number of requests per page low, even over HTTP/2.
lines: Keep requests per page few, HTTP/2 or not: one SVG sprite or inline SVG instead of a file per icon, stylesheets bundled at build time, and no reference to a file that answers 404.
Keep cookies small and few (at most 4,096 bytes each and 20 per domain): they are sent with every request to the domain, static files included.

group: I keep the number of requests per page low, even over HTTP/2.
lines: The number of requests is not a concern on this project: do not restructure assets to save requests; still remove any reference to a file that answers 404.

group: Third-party scripts and embeds (analytics, chat, A/B tests, iframes):
label: The assistant asks me before adding one
lines: Ask before adding a third-party script or an iframe, and give its weight and the requests it adds; an embed is put behind a clickable facade or `loading="lazy"`.

group: Third-party scripts and embeds (analytics, chat, A/B tests, iframes):
label: Allowed when loaded late or on interaction
lines: A third-party script or embed never loads on the critical path: load it after the page is interactive or on the first interaction, and put an iframe behind a clickable facade or `loading="lazy"`.

group: Third-party scripts and embeds (analytics, chat, A/B tests, iframes):
label: None are allowed
lines: Never add a third-party script, widget or iframe: build the feature with the project’s own code, or stop and say what is missing.

group: Photos and other raster images are served:
label: As AVIF or WebP files produced by the build or by hand
lines: Add a photo as AVIF or WebP, compressed and no larger than its biggest displayed size; never commit a raw JPEG or PNG export for one.

group: Photos and other raster images are served:
label: Through an image CDN or the framework’s image component
lines: Serve every raster image through the project’s image CDN or image component, which picks the format and the size; never link a raw file or bypass it with a plain ``.

group: Photos and other raster images are served:
label: As they are (JPEG, PNG)
lines: Images are served as JPEG or PNG: do not add a conversion step unasked; compress a new image and size it to its biggest displayed size before adding it.

group: Every image reserves its place and loads only when it is about to be seen.
lines: Give every image an explicit `width` and `height` (or an `aspect-ratio`) so the layout does not shift, and `loading="lazy"` with `decoding="async"` when it starts off screen.
Never lazy-load the image that is the largest element of the first screen: load it at once with `fetchpriority="high"`.

group: Every image reserves its place and loads only when it is about to be seen.
lines: Lazy loading is not applied by rule: add `loading="lazy"` only where asked, and still give an image its dimensions when it would otherwise shift the layout.

group: For different screen sizes, an image comes:
label: In several widths, with `srcset` and `sizes`
lines: Give a content image several widths in `srcset` (for example 400w, 800w, 1600w) and a `sizes` that matches its real layout width, so a small screen never downloads the largest file.

group: For different screen sizes, an image comes:
label: In widths generated by the image component or CDN
lines: Let the image component or CDN generate the widths: pass it the layout size (`sizes` or its equivalent) of each image rather than writing `srcset` by hand.

group: For different screen sizes, an image comes:
label: In one size
lines: Images ship in one size: export each at about twice its largest displayed width at most, never a multi-thousand-pixel original shown at a few hundred pixels.

group: The CSS of the first screen is:
label: Inlined in the head, the rest loaded without blocking
lines: Keep the inlined critical CSS to what the first screen needs, about 14 KB at most, and load the rest without blocking rendering; never inline the whole stylesheet, which bloats the HTML and escapes the cache.

group: The CSS of the first screen is:
label: Part of stylesheets split per route by the bundler
lines: CSS is split per route: import a style from the component or route that uses it so it ships with that chunk, and keep only the styles of the app shell in the global stylesheet.

group: The CSS of the first screen is:
label: In one stylesheet for the whole app
lines: The app ships one stylesheet: keep it small since it blocks the first paint, and do not set up critical-CSS extraction or CSS splitting unasked.

group: Unused CSS is removed:
label: By the build (Tailwind, PurgeCSS, CSS Modules)
lines: The build drops unused CSS: write class names in full so it can find them (never build one by concatenating strings), and never import a whole CSS framework or theme for a few rules.

group: Unused CSS is removed:
label: By hand
lines: Nothing removes unused CSS at build time: delete the rules of a component in the same change that deletes or rewrites it, and do not leave dead selectors behind.

group: Unused CSS is removed:
label: It is not
lines: Unused CSS is not removed on this project: do not add a purge step unasked, and do not make it worse by importing a whole stylesheet for a few rules.

group: In styles, the project refuses:
label: `@import` in shipped CSS
lines: Never leave an `@import` in a stylesheet that ships: each one adds a download in series; import styles through the bundler so they are concatenated.

group: In styles, the project refuses:
label: Inline `style` attributes
lines: Do not style with the `style` attribute: it is not cached, it duplicates rules and it breaks a strict CSP; use a class, and keep `style` for a value only known at run time.

group: In styles, the project refuses:
label: CSS-in-JS computed at run time
lines: Do not add CSS-in-JS that computes styles while rendering: use styles extracted at build time.

group: In styles, the project refuses:
label: Deep or highly specific selectors
lines: Select with one simple class: no deep descendant chain, no id or `!important` to win specificity, and no rule duplicated from another component.

group: In styles, the project refuses:
label: Animations of layout properties
lines: Animate only `transform` and `opacity`; never `width`, `height`, `top`, `left` or `margin`, which force a layout on every frame and miss the 16 ms a frame has at 60 frames per second.

group: In styles, the project refuses:
label: Reading layout between DOM writes
lines: Never read layout (`offsetWidth`, `getBoundingClientRect`, `scrollTop`) between DOM writes in a loop: read everything first, then write, or do the writes in `requestAnimationFrame`.

group: The JavaScript bundle is split:
label: Per route
lines: Load every route with a dynamic `import()` (`lazy` and `Suspense` in React) so the initial bundle holds only the first page: one chunk per page on top of the shared base, and no finer split.

group: The JavaScript bundle is split:
label: Per route, plus heavy components loaded on demand
lines: Load every route with a dynamic `import()`, and also a heavy component that is not shown at once (charts, editor, map); do not split further: dozens of small chunks in cascade slow navigation down.

group: The JavaScript bundle is split:
label: By the framework, automatically
lines: The framework splits the code per route: follow its conventions and its performance guide, use its dynamic import only for a heavy component hidden at first, and do not configure chunks by hand.

group: The JavaScript bundle is split:
label: It is not split
lines: The app ships as one bundle: do not introduce code splitting unasked; say so when a change adds a large library that only one screen uses.

group: The weight a dependency adds to the bundle is checked before it is added.
lines: Before adding a front-end dependency, check what it adds to the bundle and whether it tree-shakes, prefer a platform API or a lighter library, and import only the functions used, never the whole package.
Judge a script by its uncompressed size too: that is what the browser parses and runs, and it costs most on a phone.

group: The weight a dependency adds to the bundle is checked before it is added.
lines: Bundle weight does not decide the choice of a library here: pick the one that fits the task; still import only what is used.

group: No task may hold the main thread for more than 50 ms.
lines: Keep every task on the main thread under 50 ms: split long work into chunks that yield to the browser, move heavy computation to a Web Worker, and debounce or throttle handlers of scroll, resize and typing.

group: No task may hold the main thread for more than 50 ms.
lines: Do not add a worker or task chunking unasked; point out a synchronous computation that visibly freezes an interaction.

group: Web fonts are:
label: Hosted with the app
lines: Serve fonts from the app’s own origin, in WOFF2 only, and preload only the weight the first screen uses, with `as="font"`, `type="font/woff2"` and `crossorigin` (without it the file is downloaded twice).

group: Web fonts are:
label: Loaded from a font service
lines: Fonts come from a font service: keep a `<link rel="preconnect" crossorigin>` to its file domain, request only the weights and character sets in use, and do not add a second font origin.

group: Web fonts are:
label: Not used: system fonts only
lines: The project uses system fonts only: never add a web font, an icon font or a link to a font service; use the existing system font stack.

group: While a web font loads, text is shown with `font-display`:
label: `swap`: fallback at once, replaced when the font arrives
lines: Declare every `@font-face` with `font-display: swap`, and tune the fallback font with `size-adjust` so the swap does not shift the layout.

group: While a web font loads, text is shown with `font-display`:
label: `optional`: the font only if it is already there
lines: Declare every `@font-face` with `font-display: optional`: the layout must look right in the fallback font, since a first visit may never show the web font.

group: While a web font loads, text is shown with `font-display`:
label: `fallback`: short wait, replaced only if fast
lines: Declare every `@font-face` with `font-display: fallback`, and tune the fallback font with `size-adjust` so a late swap does not shift the layout.

group: I keep font families and weights few and light.
lines: Keep all fonts under 300 KB in total, with at most two families and four weights; ask before adding a family or a weight, and subset each file to the characters in use with `unicode-range`.

group: I keep font families and weights few and light.
lines: Use the families and weights the design asks for; still ship each one as a single WOFF2 file and never preload them all.

group: HTTP caching of the front end’s files is:
label: Hashed assets cached for a year, HTML always revalidated
lines: Serve hashed assets with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` and `index.html` with `no-cache` and an `ETag`; never give the HTML a long cache: it would point to bundles that no longer exist.
Reference every asset through the bundler so its name carries a content hash; a file with a fixed name (in `public/`) must not get the one-year cache.

group: HTTP caching of the front end’s files is:
label: Set by the hosting platform
lines: The hosting platform sets the cache headers: do not override them in code or configuration, and reference every asset through the bundler so its name carries a content hash.

group: HTTP caching of the front end’s files is:
label: Not set up
lines: Cache headers are not set up: do not add any unasked, and never assume a deployed file is refreshed or kept by the browser.

group: HTML, CSS and JavaScript are compressed:
label: By the CDN or the reverse proxy (Brotli, gzip)
lines: The CDN or the proxy compresses text with Brotli, then gzip: do not compress in application code, and check that a new text type (JSON, SVG, source map) is in its list of compressed types.

group: HTML, CSS and JavaScript are compressed:
label: At build time, as `.br` and `.gz` files
lines: The build writes `.br` and `.gz` files next to each text asset: keep that step when changing the build, and keep the server serving them with the right `Content-Encoding`.

group: HTML, CSS and JavaScript are compressed:
label: Not set up
lines: Text assets are served uncompressed: do not add compression unasked, and say so when a change ships a large text file.

group: Resource hints the pages use:
label: `preconnect` to critical origins (API, CDN, fonts)
lines: Add a `<link rel="preconnect">` for an origin the first screen needs (API, CDN, fonts) when introducing one, with `crossorigin` when it serves fonts; keep them to a handful and remove the hint with the origin.

group: Resource hints the pages use:
label: `dns-prefetch` to secondary origins
lines: Use `<link rel="dns-prefetch">` for an origin that is used later or only sometimes, rather than a full `preconnect`.

group: Resource hints the pages use:
label: `preload` of first-screen resources
lines: Preload only what the first screen needs and the browser finds late (the largest image, the heading font), with the right `as`; every extra preload competes with critical resources.

group: Resource hints the pages use:
label: None
lines: The pages use no resource hint: do not add `preconnect`, `dns-prefetch` or `preload` tags unasked.

group: `memo`, `useMemo` and `useCallback` are written:
label: Only where a profile shows a costly re-render
lines: Add `memo`, `useMemo` or `useCallback` only where the React DevTools Profiler shows a costly re-render with stable props; comparing props has a cost, so do not wrap by default, and remove one that no longer pays.

group: `memo`, `useMemo` and `useCallback` are written:
label: Never by hand: the React Compiler does it
lines: The React Compiler memoizes: do not write `memo`, `useMemo` or `useCallback` by hand, and follow the Rules of React (no mutation of props or state, no side effect while rendering) so it can optimize a component.

group: `memo`, `useMemo` and `useCallback` are written:
label: By default on components and callbacks passed down
lines: Wrap a component that receives props in `memo`, and pass it objects and callbacks kept stable with `useMemo` and `useCallback`; an inline object or function in its props defeats the memoization.

group: Long lists and tables are:
label: Virtualized (TanStack Virtual, react-window…)
lines: Render a list or a table that can exceed a few hundred rows with the project’s virtualization library, so only the visible rows (about 30) are in the DOM; give each row a stable `key`.

group: Long lists and tables are:
label: Paginated
lines: Never render a collection in full: page it on the server and show one page at a time; do not add a virtualization library unasked.

group: Long lists and tables are:
label: Rendered whole: they stay short
lines: Lists are short and rendered whole: do not add virtualization or pagination unasked; say so when a list can grow past a few hundred rows.

group: State lives as close as possible to the components that use it.
lines: Keep state in the lowest component that needs it: never the value of a form field in a global store or context; split a context whose value changes often, since every consumer re-renders with it.
Fetch data next to the component that shows it and subscribe to the fields it reads; poll no more often than needed, pause while the tab is hidden, and never poll at the top of the tree.

group: State lives as close as possible to the components that use it.
lines: State may be lifted or made global for convenience; still keep a value that changes on every keystroke or every second out of a context the whole page consumes.
